lines.text: [almost a whisper, holding back] In seven days... I don't make it.
[dry, a little wry] He'd pulled me off that curb, caught his bus... and left his umbrella behind.
[thinking it through, matter-of-fact] A receipt in the strap. Same bakery, six-twenty, every morning.
lines.show: A receipt in the strap. Same bakery, 6:20, every morning.

lines.text: [dry, quietly certain] People who buy bread at the same hour every day don't live far from where they buy it.
[low, tense] So I walked every lane around it. Almost eleven, there he was. Waiting, like he knew.
[softly, a little amazed] You followed a bus in the rain. For an umbrella.
The name stitched inside the strap said Arjun.
[practical, kind] You're soaked. I'll make tea.
A photograph, turned to face the wall.
[low, unsettled] He'd said that to me before. In a message. From a night he hasn't lived yet.
[barely steady] Eleven eleven. A new message. From him.
[low, frightened] He was standing right in front of me. He hadn't touched his phone.
